alex: I'm taking primary for the next 8h. quick note: maya will be secondary until 18:00 UTC, then jordan takes over. there's a small coverage gap Sat 02:00-03:00 UTC (no one in APAC) — plan ahead for any noisy jobs or deploys.

maya: noted. thanks. leaving a short cheat-sheet for common triage steps for the shift so people don't have to dig thru the full runbooks mid-page. paste any additions.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE: P2 - inference-service elevated latency (auto-detected). link: https://pager.redwood.com/p/INC-18055

alex: first quick checklist (top of mind):
- confirm customer impact: check /internal/alerts/customer-facing (or run the quick query in console)
- look at recent deploys: /eng-releases for any merges in last 30m
- check SLO dashboards (Console > per-route latency) and per-model tail latencies

jordan: adding runbook links:
- inference latency triage: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency
- kv-cache / cold-starts: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-issues
- autoscaler and capacity: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-failures

sam: quick commands I use often (copy/paste in emergencies):
```
# tail logs for the inference runtime (last 500 lines)
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/inference-runtime --tail=500

# restart deployment safely (graceful pod bounce)
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime

# scale worker pool if queue backlog high
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/inference-runtime --replicas=6
```

alex: targeted mitigations (order matters):
1) if latency spike and CPU bound: bump replicas (scale up) for immediate relief. watch load and queue length.
2) if memory/GPU OOMs present: cordon affected node(s) and trigger rollout to move pods off them; disable autoscaling for a short window if it's thrashing.
3) if model KV cache miss storms after deploy: revert or force-cache-warm using `cache-warm` job (see runbook).
4) if persistent tail latency on one model version: route traffic to a compatible fallback model (use routing policy in Console -> Routing -> Fallbacks).

maya: examples for safe rollback and fallback route (from the runbook):
```
# rollback to last stable model version
redwoodctl models rollback --model-id "m-infer-42" --to-version "v1.3.2"

# create a temporary routing rule via API
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"route": "/chat", "model": "m-infer-42:v1.3.1", "weight": 100}' \
  https://console.redwood.com/api/routing/rules
```

alex: customer comms quick pointers:
- if >5% error rate or >2x latency SLO for 15m+, escalate P1 and prep a short public blurb: 1-2 sentences: cause (investigating), affected surface (API / embeddings / streaming), mitigation in flight, ETA for update.
- paste link to status page draft in #support-incidents.

jordan: coverage gaps: for the Sat 02-03 UTC window we should avoid planned risky infra changes; set deploy freeze in releases calendar and add a page-on-call if expected traffic spike.

alex: a few targeted pointers from recent incidents (lessons learned):
- prefer route-level rollbacks over full runtime restarts when model regressions occur. less blast radius.
- always check GPU memory metrics per-pod before scaling down; scaling down too fast causes OOM cascade.
- use `--wait` flags on rollout commands when you want to be sure pods come up healthy before announcing mitigations.

maya: adding a tiny checklist to paste into pages:
- what: short description (one line)
- scope: affected endpoints / customers
- impact: latency/errors/%requests
- mitigation: step we're running now
- next steps: who will own follow-up + links to runbooks/logs

oncall-bot: REMINDER: post-incident, attach perf snapshot and prompt-eval to the incident in PagerDuty for regression monitoring.

sam: final note — here's a tiny curated list of runbook anchors for the top-4 recurring problems (copy into your notes):
- inference-latency: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency#quick-steps
- kv-cache: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-issues#warm-and-flush
- autoscaler: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-failures#manual-scale
- model-fallback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-fallbacks#create-temporary-rule

alex: perfect. i'll pin this thread to the channel and add it to the oncall doc. if anyone wants anything else added (common knobs, contact lists), drop it here. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — cc @jordan on the Sat gap so we can confirm deploy freeze.

jordan: acknowledged. i'll put a calendar hold and message releases.

sam: saved to my local cheats. thanks folks. :coffee:
